 JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .6,50,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 07.08.2021 at about 12.00 Noon, when he was driving Auto bearing Regn.No.KA-52-9579 along with his wife and daughter on left side of road, on NH-75,
Kunigal-Nelamangala Road, Opp. Bhavani Shanker House, Hanchipura Gate, Kasaba Hobli,
Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, at that time the offending Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly took on right side and caused accident.

Due to which, he sustained grievous injuries and thereafter he was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent Rs.50,000/- towards medicine, treatment, conveyances, nourishment and attendant charges.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was working as a driver and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver.
The respondents being the RC owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal hence, he has been placed as ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal and filed his written statement.

4. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 has filed counter to petition by denying the petition averments.
It has further disputed the manner of accident, age of injured and quantum of compensation claimed under different heads.

Further contended that according to FIR, driver cum owner of autorickshaw was proceeding along with his wife and child on Bhavani Shankar House Hanchipura Gate, at that time one lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 its driver without any signal taken vehicle right side of road and the driver of autorickshaw not avoided accident and dashed to the lorry petrol tank and fell down all the persons and sustained grievous injuries.
Driver of lorry was taken all cautions with signal but the petitioner without observing the indication and Sri.Chikkaraju.

H.C vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31265922/
2 high speed running vehicle and selflessly dashed to lorry and sustained injuries.
Further contended that the autorickshaw cab driver cum owner was having the permit to Nelamangala Rural Area and but alleged accident occurred out of permit limits and autorickshaw cab was driving on NH-75 Road by violating permit.

Further contended that the autorickshaw cab driver cum owner was holding DL to non transport and the M.V.No.KA-52-9579 Autorickshaw Cab/Passenger vehicle is transport vehicle, but he was not holding the badge at the time of accident.

Further contended that the 1 st respondent is insured with this respondent under policy No.171001/31/20/P114635690 valid from 18.03.2021 to 17.03.2022 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 07.08.2021 at about 12.00 noon, on NH-75, Kunigal-Nelamangala Road,
Opp Bhavani Shankar House, Hanchipura Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk,
Bengaluru Rural District, when he was driving a Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-52- 9579, due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing registration No.TN-29-BB-3922 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

6. In order to prove case of petitioner, petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and Dr.Nagaraj.B.N.
examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and closed his side of evidence.
The respondents have not led any evidence either oral or documentary.
7. I have heard the arguments from both sides and perused the material available on record.

-:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:-
It is the case of petitioner that due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending lorry, the accident occurred.
The petitioner alleged that the lorry all of a sudden took towards right side, as a result the accident occurred.
The petitioner gave statement before the police in hospital as per Ex.P2 by alleging that due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle the accident occurred.
The police have registered the case as per Ex.P.1 and thereafter the police went near the place of accident and drew up mahazar as per Ex.P.4 by narrating the place of accident.
As per mahazar, the accident occurred on National Highway in between auto and lorry.
PW.1 in his chief examination deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending lorry the accident occurred.
Even in his cross examination he has deposed that due to negligence on the part of driver of lorry the accident occurred.
On meticulous perusal of evidence of PW.1, the respondent insurance company nothing elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.

The police after thorough investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending lorry for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
10.

The learned counsel for respondent insurance company vehemently argued that the Air Cab belongs to petitioners holding the permit to Nelamangala rural 5 K.M radius, but the petitioner violated permit conditions , he was going to Tumkur District Hebbur i.e., 50 Kms, but authority issued permit only rural area of 5 Kms and auto was running on National Highway.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police Station have filed charge sheet only against the lorry.
Further the learned counsel for respondent insurance company vehemently argued RTO Nelamangala issued permit to auto to ply in rural limits of Nelamangala.
The accident occurred on National Highway and not on service road, as such petitioner violated the permit conditions.
11. PW.1 in his cross examination, he has deposed that he was going from Hebbur to Nelamangala and he himself was driving the auto.
Further he has deposed that the permit was given within the radius of 5 Kms of Nelamangala Rural.

Further in his cross examination, he has deposed that he has seen the lorry which was parked 20 feet away from him, the lorry all of a sudden took towards right side as a result there was an accident.
After investigation police filed charge sheet against the driver of offending Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29- BB-3922.
In charge sheet it is alleged that the driver of lorry without observing the vehicle negligently took his lorry towards right side as a result the accident occurred.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.5 - Sketch, the accident occurred on National Highway in the middle of road.
Even in IMV Report mentioned the damages to auto and lorry.
As per Ex.P.8 - IMV Report, the right side rear wheel mudguard and lorry fuel tank right side dented.
Ex.P.8 IMV Report corroborates the case of petitioner.
The I.O has not alleged that there was a negligence on the part of petitioner, it clearly alleged that due to negligence on the part of offending lorry the accident occurred.
Now the contention of respondent insurance that the auto violated the permit conditions.
As per I.O. and case of petitioner the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of offending lorry.
The respondent insurance company nothing placed before the tribunal to show that only due to negligence on the part of petitioner the accident occurred.

Only on the basis of violation of permit by the petitioner the respondent cannot escape from his liability, because the accident occurred only due to negligence on the part of driver of offending lorry.

The respondent insurance company has not placed any materials before the tribunal to show that the insured lorry violated Sri.Chikkaraju.H.C vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31265922/
4 terms and conditions of policy.
So, under such circumstances the respondent insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

On perusal of all the police and hospital documents placed by the petitioner, it is evident that there was a road traffic accident and in the said accident petitioner has sustained grievous injuries due to rash and negligent driving of driver of lorry.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.9, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., let me discussion one by one.
(i) Towards injury and pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries caused to him,
petitioner has produced wound certificate issued by Nelamangala Taluk Hospital marked at Ex.P.3, wherein it discloses that the injuries sustained by petitioner are grievous in nature.
So, on perusal of records he took treatment in hospital as an inpatient and the petitioner examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.17 and Ex.P.18.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and he assessed the disability for right arm at 33% and for whole body at 11%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.55,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital.
The petitioner has also produced 4 Medical bills marked at Ex.P.12 for Rs.3,800/- and one medical prescription marked at Ex.P.13.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.3,800/- is just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges: On perusal of the records, the accident occurred on 07.08.2021 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was inpatient at Hospital as he has sustained injuries.

So,
during the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment.
The petitioner has not produced discharge summary to show how many days he has taken treatment.
By Considering the facts and circumstance of the case the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .1,000/- is just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
Sri. Chikkaraju.

5
(iv) Towards Conveyance:

The petitioner is the resident of Bannikuppe, Singanahalli Post, Hebbur Hobli,
Tumkur Taluk, Tumkur District and he has admitted for treatment at Hospital.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has not produced discharge summary.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.10,000/- is just and proper towards conveyance charges.
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:
The petitioner has contended that he was working as a driver and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
In order to prove his income, the petitioner has not produce any documents to show that he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In the absence of positive documents regarding his occupation and income, this tribunal will consider notional income.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner might have not attended his regular work at least for a period of 2 months.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2021 at Rs.15,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok Adalat.

So, in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to the Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
Case on hand the petitioner has not produced any relevant document to prove his income.
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2021 treated as Rs.15,000/- per month as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- (15,000/- x 2) towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Permanent Disability:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was inpatient in hospital, and sustained permanent disablement.

The petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N.
working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center Hospital, examined as PW.2.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.
The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained Right shoulder comminuted greater tuberosity with displacement and he was treated conservatively.
The doctor has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and he assessed the disability for right arm at 33% and to the whole body at 11%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.17 & 18 i.e., clinical report and recent X-ray film.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.

Therefore,
considering all these aspects, the functional disability is assessed at 9%.

In order to prove age of the petitioner, he has produced Ex.P.10 & 11 - Notarized copy of Driving License and Aadhaar Card, wherein date of birth is mentioned as 20.02.1991 and accident occurred on 07.08.2021, so the age of petitioner was 31 years as on the date of accident.

Hence, the same is taken into consideration for Sri.Chikkaraju.H.C vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31265922/
6
applying multiplier and multiplier '16' is applicable as per Smt. Sarla Verma case.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble supreme court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

entities.text: Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (15,000/- x 12) = Rs.1,80,000/- Loss of future earning p.a. (9% of prior annual income) Rs.16,200/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 16 Loss of future earnings - (Rs.16,200/-
x 16)= Rs.2,59,200/-.
The petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,59,200/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:- The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day-today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

13. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

14.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
Sri.Chikkaraju.H.C vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31265922/
7 interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
15. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 by its driver.
The police authorities have not filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.181 of M.V.Act.
So, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .3,69,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Sixty Nine Thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Sri. Chikkaraju.
